pr_body:
The main objective of this PR is to address the linked issue below. The main changes in this PR include:
- `LocalHealthMonitor`: to allow for a more "scalable" setup, I added the abstract class `HealthCheck<T>`, which represents a health check that will be performed on every node, and made `LocalHealthMonitor` work with a list of `HealthCheck`s. This reduces future effort to add new health checks.
  - Also extracted `DiskCheck` to a separate class/file.
  - And added `RepositoriesCheck` for this new feature.
- `RepositoryIntegrityHealthIndicatorService`: refactored this class to do a more extensive analysis of the repository health in the cluster.
- Field additions, new `TransportVersion`, constructor updates, etc.

Fixes #103784
pr_title: Extend `repository_integrity` health indicator for unknown and invalid repos
pr_comment: Hi @nielsbauman, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

review_comment: I would also add the dsl health info here for completeness.
We use this list in two places (potentially) with `limitSize()`. If we sort it here then it can be nicely stable in both places.
I think we should initialise this in each test so it's closer to the code that uses it. What do you think?

I implemented it this way because I needed to have a non-empty map of repositories health info to avoid the repo analyzer class complaining that the status was "unknown". Therefore, I chose to create a "green" health info before each test so every test has the same "green" starting position. Do you still think it makes more sense to move the health info initialization to the tests themselves?
Hm, so I do not think we should fake the starting point. Should we reconsider keeping the health green when there are missing health information, to avoid having the lag upon restart?

I copied that approach from the [DiskHealthIndicatorService.java](https://github.com/nielsbauman/elasticsearch/blob/f2552321a46ea948f2146b821c65c58d84e9fabd/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/health/node/DiskHealthIndicatorService.java#L87-L87). I think it makes sense to keep the status to unknown when there is missing information (either due to startup or some other cause); that feels more accurate to me. What do you think?

We have been going back on forth on this honestly. For DSL we decided to start with `GREEN` mainly because it would take even longer to get an answer since DSL only runs every 5 minutes.

It is more accurate but it's also more noisy, that's why you see us considering. The reason is that `unknown` is "higher" than `green` during merging so it takes over the overall status.

We can keep the unknown here too, to be inline with the disk indicator and maybe bring back the topic if we see that it's too noisy. Or maybe we should re-evaluate the strategy for merging. What do you think?
I think I'm a fan of the current merging strategy, but I do understand the noise concern. I'd be in favour of keeping this approach, and keeping an eye out for any reports regarding this.
Please add javadoc.
I think we need to add here the repository health info as well, right?
Here as well the name of the repo.
Since we are here, we should sort `corruptedRepositories` too.
Nit: I would prefer to leave this here so the `nodeId` is the first field we assign.
Shouldn't we be checking the repo health info just like we are asserting the disk health info, see line 92 (current code)?
Out of curiosity why did you choose to inline this?

I initially did that because I added the anchors to the links (and thought it would save some memory by not constructing the help URLs but inlining them), but I forgot to extract the constant after I removed the anchor. Good catch, thanks
Any objections to adding javadoc here too?

I would still keep this as a first step. If a user doesn't have repositories we should immediately respond that it's green. It will reduce also the object creation for no reason such as creating iterators and so on.
We could add a javadoc here, it's not a very obvious method.

I usually don't write javadoc for methods that override a method (unless the method does something considerably different than its parent). Do you think it still makes sense to add javadoc here, considering that the parent method does have javadoc?
Good point, yes, as long there is nothing extra add sounds good!
I think javadoc would be helpful here.
I didn't add it because I thought the method name + param names + small & clear body would be sufficient, but I'll add some javadoc 👍🏻 .
Nice, I didn't know about this.
I think javadoc would be helpful here.

I think we can explain here how it helps us. For example:

> We use the previous observed value to verify that no other concurrent process has updated the health check's value.

Food for thought.... I just realise that we might have a race here, can you think along with me on the following scenario and its implications:

- Last reported value was null
- there is new health node
- New run starts the update process and records previous value `null`
- health node/master change
- new reported value is `null`
- Run sees null and considers that it's ok to update the value.... 

What do you think?

Hm I think you might be right. The only workaround I can think of right now is to have some kind of ref counter that increments every time we send a request, so we can be 100% sure there weren't any other requests sent while waiting for the response of the first request. That way, the last step you mentioned won't be executed, as the ref counter doesn't match, so we're not updating any `lastReportedValue`s as we know there's already another request on its way. I think that implementation should also be doable, what do you think?
Yes, I was thinking something like that too. A versioned "last value". We can also open an issue and address it in a follow up PR.
